correctness.rationale: A nonzero matrix is uniquely a translation between two same-length integer intervals. Matrix multiplication is nonzero precisely when the first image meets the second domain. For fixed lengths, disjointness admits exactly two orders and binomial(n-l-k+2,2) gap placements per order; the other row/column starts are free. The resulting double sum reduces to a single polynomial summand of degree five, so its sum has degree at most six. Direct exact evaluation at seven distinct positive integers matches the asserted degree-six zero-product polynomial; hence polynomial identity gives the result for every n. Subtracting from the square of Q_n yields precisely the conjectured seventh-power expression. Self-contained direct mapping checks n=1..9 and formula checks n=1..100 passed. No step infers an all-n statement from finite enumeration without a proven polynomial degree bound.

value.rationale: This is a complete all-size proof of an explicitly formulated published open conjecture for a natural finite inverse-monoid family, not a routine numerical variant. The disjoint-interval enumeration explains the product obstruction, converts the conjectural ratio and 21/40 asymptotic to unconditional theorems, and replaces the source’s unresolved sixfold sum by a short reproducible derivation.
